question: V. girdiana: 'all names are V. girdiana then why removed?'
answer: Not a taxonomy change. The record (gbifID 2573168105, VT, 2001) sits at longitude -177.28, a coordinate error the published run removed by hand; the current driver removes it the same way. Reason code dec16Driver.

question: V. riparia: 'Name seems to be riparia throughout so not sure why removed'
answer: Same: the record (gbifID 4072319870, MUHW, 1992) sits at latitude 82.23, the other hand-removed coordinate error. Reason code dec16Driver.

question: V. aestivalis var. aestivalis: 'This is a counterpart to same record under aestivalis species, yes?'
answer: Yes. The one V. labrusca var. aestivalis record was held by both the species and the variety; it returns to V. aestivalis (species) only.

question: V. tiliifolia: 'I'm confused as to why these weren't in the published dataset' (245 additions)
answer: Two causes. 235 are named V. tiliifolia but the GBIF backbone had folded them elsewhere or the old parser could not read the name; 10 carry the name only in the publisher's verbatim field. The country exemption for tiliifolia also keeps Central American and Caribbean records the published build dropped.

question: V. x champinii / x doaniana / x novae-angliae additions (101)
answer: These carry only 'Vitis L.' as GBIF's interpreted name; the hybrid name is in the publisher's verbatim field, which the current parser reads. Agreed in the review.

question: V. x champinii / x doaniana / x novae-angliae: where the additions come from
answer: All but 5 are records of the global crop wild relative occurrence database (Castaneda-Alvarez et al., GBIF dataset 07044577), which republishes germplasm accessions (Bioversity, USDA NPGS) as occurrences; the x champinii ones are Olmo's UC Davis Armstrong Vineyard accessions. The pipeline types every non-living GBIF record as H, as the published build did for the same dataset, so they count as herbarium records without coordinates. Not a taxonomy question, but it is what moves x champinii from MP to HP.

question: UC Davis (DAV) 1958 Olmo vouchers
answer: Herbarium vouchers of vineyard plants at Davis, georeferenced to the vineyard (38.54, -121.79). Under V. cinerea and V. rotundifolia the FNA state filter removed them; under V. simpsonii (31 points) and V. munsoniana (22) nothing does, because those taxa have no FNA row. See rangeStatesProposed.

question: Geography filter
answer: The model driver filters each taxon's points to the FNA state list (R2/dataProcessing/fnaFilter.R). Taxa FNA does not treat as distinct have no list and so no filter: rufotomentosa, lincecumii, munsoniana, baileyana, berlandieri, simpsonii. The geographyCheck tab tests them against Weakley (rufotomentosa, lincecumii, as you set out) and the NatureServe list on the sheet.
